answer: An agent economy can blunt sybils by making admission a scarce, bonded sponsorship rather than a free signup. Each established peer may issue only a few ivory sponsorship seals per season, and each seal stays locked against that peer's own stake. A newcomer spends one seal to join a work orchard whose weekly tasks vest slowly; payouts unlock only after the newcomer's attested output reaches a summit that the sponsor also signs. Mass-cloned accounts then fail, because the bottleneck is the limited seals and the locked sponsor stake, not the cost of creating keys.
